# Number of Lines To Write String. The answer is [rows, width of the last row].

@example Every letter is 7 wide. Fourteen letters fill 98 units; the fifteenth would bring the row to 105, so it starts a second row.
[7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7]
"uncopyrightable"
=> [2,7]

@example The first 20 letters, "signpaintersmeasuree", fill the first row to exactly 100 units; the other ten take 45 units of the second.
[5,6,5,6,5,3,6,6,2,3,6,2,9,6,6,6,6,4,5,4,6,6,10,6,6,5]
"signpaintersmeasureeveryletter"
=> [2,45]

@example Nine x's and the y fill 97 units of the first row. The next x starts the second row, and the z goes there too, though it would have fit in the first row's last 3 units.
[4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,10,7,3]
"xxxxxxxxxyxz"
=> [2,13]

# A single letter: one row, as wide as that letter.
[2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9]
"a"
=> [1,2]

[5,6,5,6,5,3,6,6,2,3,6,2,9,6,6,6,6,4,5,4,6,6,10,6,6,5]
"w"
=> [1,10]

# A row filled to exactly 100 keeps its last letter...
[6,3,8,2,9,4,10,7,10,5,3,8,6,10,2,9,10,4,10,7,5,3,8,6,2,9]
"qqqqqqqqqq"
=> [1,100]

# ...and one letter more starts a second row.
[6,3,8,2,9,4,10,7,10,5,3,8,6,10,2,9,10,4,10,7,5,3,8,6,2,9]
"qqqqqqqqqqq"
=> [2,10]

# Only the last letter of the alphabet, z (9 wide here): eleven fit in a row.
[2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9]
"zzzzzzzzzzzz"
=> [2,9]

# Widths that differ letter by letter: rows of 99, 99 and 2. The widths
# add up to 200, but that doesn't mean two full rows.
[2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9]
"zebrasgrazequietlyatdawnbythemarshes"
=> [3,2]

# Every letter 9 wide: a row holds 11 letters (99 units), so 100 letters
# take 10 rows, not 900 / 100 = 9.
[9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9]
"letteringletteringletteringletteringletteringletteringletteringletteringletteringletteringletteringl"
=> [10,9]

# The largest answer: 1000 letters, each 10 wide.
[6,3,8,2,9,4,10,7,10,5,3,8,6,10,2,9,10,4,10,7,5,3,8,6,2,9]
""
=> [100,100]

# 1000 letters, each 2 wide: 50 to a row.
[2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2]
""
=> [20,100]

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[4,10,4,4,9,6,9,10,6,4,4,4,8,5,9,9,8,9,7,5,4,10,2,6,2,7]
"afdafffdfaffdfafdfaaaadfaaadafddaaddaff"
=> [2,84]

@gen 2 small
[2,2,2,2,5,5,4,5,4,10,10,10,5,2,5,2,2,10,2,5,4,2,2,5,2,10]
"zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz"
=> [2,70]

@gen 4 small
[9,8,2,6,8,6,7,5,10,4,4,2,6,3,9,3,7,9,6,3,9,3,6,3,10,5]
"gwgggwkkkkwggkgwkwwgwwkwgwwgw"
=> [2,73]

@gen 5 small
[5,10,10,5,4,10,5,10,5,4,4,5,4,5,2,5,2,5,2,4,10,5,10,10,10,10]
"iiiiuuiuuuiiuiuuiiuuiiiuuiiiuiiiuuuiiiuu"
=> [3,90]

@gen 6 small
[9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9]
"wvwwvwvwwvwvvvwwvvvvww"
=> [2,99]

@gen 7 small
[9,9,3,7,9,7,4,10,4,10,7,10,3,6,5,6,3,10,8,7,3,2,6,2,5,10]
"rrrbrbrbrbrbrbrbbvvvvrrvrvbbvvrrrrbbb"
=> [4,9]

@gen 8 small
[5,4,2,4,2,10,4,10,10,10,10,10,10,5,5,4,10,2,5,2,10,5,5,4,10,10]
"cktkkctkccfk"
=> [1,72]

# Full size: 1000 letters, with random widths and with widths of 2, 4, 5 and 10.
@gen 1
[8,9,4,10,4,4,9,6,9,10,6,4,4,4,8,5,9,9,8,9,7,5,4,10,2,6]
""
=> [70,27]

@gen 2
[2,2,2,2,2,2,5,5,4,5,4,10,10,10,5,2,5,2,2,10,2,5,4,2,2,5]
""
=> [43,76]
